intro.title: Implement KeysMatching type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom TypeScript utility type called `KeysMatching`. This type will filter the keys of an object to only include those whose values match a specified type. The core concept involves using mapped types and conditional types to iterate over object keys and check their value types. You will work with keyof, extends, and indexed access types to implement this logic. By the end, you will understand how to create reusable type utilities that enhance type safety in your TypeScript projects.
intro.usecase: The `KeysMatching` type is essential for building type-safe data filtering and selection components in real-world applications. For example, in a product dashboard with a dynamic filter panel, you need to ensure that a user can only select filter keys that correspond to numeric columns (like 'price' or 'inventory') for a range slider, not text-based ones. This pattern allows TypeScript to enforce that a 'filterByNumericKey' prop can only accept keys of the data object whose values are numbers, preventing runtime errors. It's commonly used in component libraries for tables, advanced search interfaces, and configuration panels where UI controls must be dynamically bound to specific, type-appropriate properties of a data model.
